chunks: Yūnus, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning
A man who said to his wife, “You did not come to me as a virgin.” He عليه السلام said: “There is nothing upon him, because virginity may go away without intercourse.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His statement عليه السلام, “There is nothing upon him,” means that there is no complete hadd punishment upon him, even though there may still be taʿzīr upon him according to what was contained in the first report.

key_terms.الْخَبَرُ الْأَوَّلُ: the first report previously cited on the issue
key_terms.الْعُذْرَةَ: virginity or the physical sign associated with it
key_terms.تَعْزِيرٌ: a discretionary punishment imposed by judicial authority

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man tells his wife that she was not a virgin when he married her?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling regarding a husband who tells his wife that she did not come to him as a virgin. The Imam عليه السلام states that no complete hadd punishment applies, because the loss of virginity can occur without intercourse; al-Shaykh clarifies that discretionary punishment may still apply based on other evidence.
